citation.title: Predicting disruptive instabilities in controlled fusion plasmas through deep learning
citation.authors: Kates-Harbeck, J.; Svyatkovskiy, A.; Tang, W.

topic: Disruption prediction on DIII-D and JET with a CNN plus LSTM model, using scalar signals and profiles
own_question: Can deep learning give disruption alarms 30 ms before the event, including on a machine not used for training?
actual_method_and_evidence: The model is trained on archival shots resampled to a 1 ms grid using the last known value. Signals that are time-centred filtered are shifted so the model sees no future data. Results are offline AUCs compared against gradient-boosted trees and other classical models. There is no CES, ion-temperature, BES or ECEI-voltage nowcasting, and no closed-loop deployment.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Earlier tokamak machine-learning work enforced causality by resampling to the last known value and time-shifting noncausally filtered database signals.
claim_checks.qualification: This was offline archival preprocessing for disruption alarms. It says nothing about CES report timing.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: The target is a disruption label at a 30 ms deadline. This is event forecasting, not current-report nowcasting.
validation_if_relevant: Random shot splits are used for DIII-D. JET is evaluated with a carbon-wall to ITER-like-wall split. Cross-machine tests are also reported.
forbidden_inferences: It does not validate CES or impurity Ti nowcasting.
Its offline AUCs do not imply real-time feasibility for our task.
It does not show that prior work generally ignored causality.
Its profile-importance result does not transfer to BES/ECEI incremental information.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional citation only, as a precedent for causal preprocessing of fusion time series. The task, targets and diagnostics differ from our study.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
